TRUST-02.reason: Neptune does not implement an SFTP or SSH client or store a host-key trust database; remote storage transport and fingerprint verification are owned by Saturn.

TRUST-07.reason: Neptune consumes typed project and producer credentials but does not register an external provider webhook or pass a webhook secret to a provider; those trust boundaries belong to the provider integration service.

HLT-07.reason: Neptune does not own the remote storage credential or root and cannot perform an SFTP read-write-delete canary; Saturn owns that storage capability probe while Neptune reports transfer outcomes separately.

INT-09.reason: Neptune is a backup and synchronization agent with a local socket API; it does not own a chat command gateway, provider command menu, reply keyboard, aliases, or conversational state machine.

INT-10.reason: Neptune polls Saturn over outbound HTTPS and does not register Telegram or other external-provider webhooks; it owns no provider callback activation lifecycle.

INT-11.reason: Neptune accepts scoped commands through an authenticated Saturn poll and has no external webhook ingestion queue, repository or tenant filter, provider delivery worker, or callback ping.

DATA-05.reason: Neptune sends archives to Saturn over authenticated HTTP and owns no storage account or namespace in which to execute a remote write-read-delete canary; Saturn performs the storage capability probe.

DATA-10.reason: Independent storage accounts and failure domains are external Saturn deployment resources; Neptune exports one scoped archive and cannot establish remote storage independence by itself.
